name: issue_827_missing_forecast_fallback_escalates
description: Issue #827 GAP-2 / #1066 (Design D nearest-edge arming, docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f). A warm-day zone with thermal-model confidence 'medium' but no cached floor-crossing prediction (a missing forecast for the cycle) must still defend the floor: indoor 65F, 3F below comfort_heat(68), arms heat on the first evaluation. The family decision reads only indoor versus the band; thermal confidence and any cached floor-crossing time are not inputs, so the 'guard cannot decide' dead end of the original GAP-2 cannot exist. The harness always passes comfort_floor_crossing_time=None, so this is the normal default state here.
source: Issue #827 Design table, GAP-2 — a non-none-confidence zone with a missing floor-crossing forecast previously dead-ended instead of falling back.
notes: Occupant impact: right after a model refresh (before the next prediction run repopulates the cache) the comfort floor was silently undefended in the original GAP-2. The house must get heat on the first reading below the floor regardless of prediction state.

Design D rule exercised (docs/08 section 6f): indoor < floor -> heating immediately. thermal_model (confidence medium, k_passive -0.12) is kept in the scenario to show it has no influence on the decision. The 08:32 re-evaluation is a redundant re-affirmation kept from the original timeline; final-state assertions cannot prove WHEN heating was armed (timing evidence: issue_1066_cold_morning_mild_day_arms_heat_immediately.json).

Near-duplicate: this scenario and issue_827_hot_day_dawn_dip_arms_heat.json have the same shape (65F vs 68F floor, single breach reading) and differ only by day type (warm here, hot there) and the thermal_model block; issue_827_off_day_floor_breach_escalates.json and issue_821_comfort_floor_fallback_no_confidence.json are the mild and no-confidence variants.

(a) Scenario effectiveness: with nearest-edge arming deleted (origin/main) a warm day is natively cooling and heat is against-grain, needing the warm deadband plus recency and a 90 s sustain across two evaluations; a regression that gated the floor defense on thermal-model confidence or a cached crossing time would leave comfort_family=cooling and fail the final assertions.
(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08 section 6f (ODE floor guard removed; thermal confidence and crossing time are not inputs).

(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: the comfort floor is undefended for stretches of time (for example right after a model refresh) and the home drifts cold with the thermostat in cool.

events.note: Warm-day classification. Base_family resolves to 'cooling' (active=ceiling). Thermal model confidence is 'medium' (not 'none'), but no comfort_floor_crossing_time is ever supplied by this harness's classification dispatch -> decide_ode_floor_guard() returns NO_BREACH_PREDICTED every cycle.
Indoor has decayed to 65F, 3F below comfort_heat(68).
First evaluation with indoor below the floor: floor breach, heat is armed immediately. No cached floor-crossing time exists, which is irrelevant to the selector.
Re-evaluation 2 minutes later: still below the floor, heating remains armed (redundant re-affirmation kept from the original timeline).

assertions.reason: Baseline: warm day, indoor within band — comfort band arms normally.

GAP-2 fix: a zone with non-none thermal confidence but no cached floor-crossing prediction still gets its floor defended. Final-state assertion; heating was armed at the first below-floor evaluation (08:30).
The escalated mode is a real climate.set_temperature/set_hvac_mode call at comfort_heat.

verdict.summary: A zone with thermal-model confidence but no cached floor-crossing prediction arms heat on the first evaluation below the comfort floor.
verdict.observed_behavior: Cooling family at 71F; the 65F reading at 08:30 arms heating and commands heat at comfort_heat.
verdict.expected_behavior: The family decision depends only on indoor versus the band, never on prediction state.
